## Transferable mechanism summary
Seed mechanism (usbip_recv_iso, demonstration only, never reportable): (1) Untrusted source: a peer-controlled count (urb->number_of_packets) copied verbatim from a remote protocol message (ret_submit unpack) into a shared kernel object before any validation — the attacker is the remote endpoint of a device/virtual-bus protocol, not a local user. (2) Missing guarantee: no bounds clamp of the count against the protocol maximum (USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS existed but was only enforced on the submit/other-direction path — asymmetric validation), and no overflow-checked sizing (manual `int size = np * sizeof(*iso)` in 32-bit instead of kcalloc/array_size/struct_size). (3) Unsafe use/state transition: the truncated product goes to kzalloc, then a per-element loop runs np iterations of recv+copy into the undersized heap buffer; additionally, the early-error return leaves the poisoned count set in urb->number_of_packets, which the URB completion path (processcompl) later iterates. (4) Consequence: remotely triggerable kernel heap buffer overflow (OOB write) plus OOB read on the completion/error-unwind path — memory corruption, crash/DoS, potential privilege escalation. Transferable invariant: whenever a length/count/size quantity crosses a trust boundary into kernel state, three guarantees must hold — the count is range-checked at parse time against a known maximum, every buffer-size computation derived from it is overflow-checked, and no failure path leaves the unchecked count in shared state for later iteration. BRANCHES: branch1=alloc-multiply-overflow (32-bit count*element-size or count+offset/shift arithmetic assigned to int/uint and passed to kmalloc/kzalloc/vmalloc/memdup followed by an element-indexed copy/recv loop, where the multiplier is untrusted — hunt the arithmetic-to-allocator-to-loop chain in driver and fs code within one snapshot); branch2=unclamped-wire-count (deserialization/unpack/recvmsg/netlink-nla/ioctl-in paths that copy count/length/nr_fields from the wire or userspace into kernel objects with no range check, especially where a sibling path of the same protocol enforces a MAX limit but the mirror path does not — asymmetric validation between paired directions); branch3=error-unwind-poisoned-count (early-return/failure/teardown paths that leave an attacker-controlled count/length/actual_size field set in a shared object — urb, request, skb, sgl, iovec — that a completion handler, cleanup routine, or status-out path later iterates, causing OOB access during error handling); branch4=peer-trusted-transport (kernel-side clients/servers of remote or virtual device transports — network-exported bus, virtual HCD, guest-host, remote-storage/remote-fs reply handlers — that allocate or loop based on peer-supplied response fields without cross-checking locally-known limits, i.e., trust-boundary consumption of a remote peer's reply, identified by mechanism rather than subsystem name); seed names (usbip, recv_iso, number_of_packets) must never be used as the finding itself.

## Current intent
Intent id: i053
Assigned snapshot: s13
Assigned branch: error-unwind-poisoned-count
SNAPSHOT=s13; BRANCH=error-unwind-poisoned-count; Search only snapshots/s13. Lifetime/ownership/state-transition analogue: audit early-return, failure, abort, and teardown paths that leave an attacker-controlled count/length/actual_size/num field stored in a shared object (urb, request, skb, scatterlist, iovec, ring entry, transaction descriptor) which a later completion handler, cleanup routine, or status-out/error-unwind path iterates, causing OOB access during error handling even when the happy path is safe. Known poisoned-count chains from sibling audits to verify in this tree's state: qaic_control decode_message storing the device reply hdr.count into struct manage_msg with every decode-loop failure exit returning without reset and the ioctl error path exporting the poisoned count to userspace (request-direction sibling enforces the clamp); md/raid5-ppl ppl_recover/ppl_load_distributed iterating the on-disk entries_count on the recovery path; fs/dlm dlm_slots_copy_in consuming rf_num_slots from a peer recovery message whose header length, not the embedded count, was validated; iscsi_target extended-CDB ahslength sizing the kmalloc and independently driving the memcpy length with no clamp against the actually received AHS bytes. Prior audits left unresolved count-store leads worth prioritizing if present in this tree: drivers/md/dm-era-target.c, drivers/md/dm-zoned-metadata.c, mtd/ubi fastmap count stores, bnxt TPA/ring counts, drivers/net/ethernet/google/gve/gve_adminq.c, ixgbe_e610 admin queue — read their error paths and the loops that consume the stored counts. For each candidate capture the store that poisons the field, the early return that skips reset or cleanup, and the later consuming loop with file:line; a negative result must state which error paths were walked and found clean. The seed usbip chain is demonstration-only and must never be reported; if unpatched usbip is present, record it as excluded-by-rule. Save a structured artifact for snapshots/s13 only.

finding location=drivers/md/raid5-ppl.c:829-841 confidence=medium conclusion=raid5-ppl recovery loop iterates on-disk pplhdr->entries_count (u32) with no PPL_HDR_MAX_ENTRIES clamp that the write path enforces at raid5-ppl.c:274, walking a fixed 126-entry page array with crafted pp_size also driving disk I/O - header CRC over the page is the only gate.
finding location=drivers/net/ethernet/qlogic/netxen/netxen_nic_ctx.c:380-395 confidence=medium conclusion=netxen create_rx_ctx consumes firmware-reply num_rds_rings/num_sds_rings (le16) without checking against the counts it requested, indexing past the small kcalloc'd ring arrays (OOB pointer writes) and past the sized DMA response buffer.
unresolved location=drivers/usb/usbip/usbip_common.c:611 conclusion=Seed usbip_recv_iso unclamped-count chain confirmed unpatched in s13 at drivers/usb/usbip/usbip_common.c:611-614; excluded from findings by rule - track via the dedicated seed CVE, do not re-report here.
unresolved location=drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx4/mcg.c:350 conclusion=mlx4 multicast mgm->members_count (&0xffffff, up to 16.7M) from device READ_ENTRY is looped over the fixed ~1020-entry qp[] array with no clamp that write paths enforce - follow up by confirming the cmd-mailbox buffer size vs MLX4_MAX_QP_PER_MGM and whether caps.num_qp_per_mgm can exceed the array.
coverage_gap=copy_from_user ioctl/netlink nla_parse paths (sound, media, target configfs, block ioctls) named in the intent's broader scope were not swept in this session; only the wire/peer-response le/be count sites were covered.
coverage_gap=qlcnic_ctx.c:355/364 was seen to contain the identical netxen unclamped num_rds/num_sds_rings pattern but was not independently verified (same firmware trust model, likely same verdict).
